`No. 1 Nebraska defeated No. 16 Penn State 3–0` (25–20, 25–17, 25–18) on Thursday, October 1, 2026, at Rec Hall in University Park, Pennsylvania.[[1]](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/nebraska-vs-penn-state-volleyball-225929260.html)[[2]](https://www.foxsportsradio1310.com/2026/10/01/how-to-watch-nebraska-vs-penn-state-volleyball-tv-channel-streaming-time-3/)[[3]](https://www.centralnebraskatoday.com/2026/10/01/no-1-huskers-sweep-no-16-penn-state/)[[4]](https://www.hastingstribune.com/husker_red_zone/top-ranked-nebraska-keeps-rolling-on-after-sweeping-no-16-penn-state/article_e150a215-74c7-43f8-8334-322ea8d80766.html)[[5]](http://www.collegian.psu.edu/sports/women_volleyball/rec-hall-feels-the-energy-in-no-16-penn-state-womens-volleyballs-loss-to-no/article_b50e42db-1caa-43df-af0e-ae4420f103c4.html)[[6]](https://www.foxsports.com/stories/collegesports/how-watch-nebraska-vs-penn-state-volleyball-tv-channel-streaming-time)

### Match Summary
The top-ranked Cornhuskers controlled the match from start to finish, outhitting the Nittany Lions .440 to .267 and outblocking them 10 to 2. Harper Murray led Nebraska with 13 kills (.414 hitting percentage), while Andi Jackson added 11 kills and a team-high seven blocks. Despite strong efforts from Penn State's Kennedy Martin (17 kills) and former Husker Whitney Lauenstein (12 kills), the Nittany Lions could not break through Nebraska's disciplined defense.[[1]](https://www.centralnebraskatoday.com/2026/10/01/no-1-huskers-sweep-no-16-penn-state/)[[2]](https://www.hastingstribune.com/husker_red_zone/top-ranked-nebraska-keeps-rolling-on-after-sweeping-no-16-penn-state/article_e150a215-74c7-43f8-8334-322ea8d80766.html)| Team | Set 1 | Set 2 | Set 3 | Final |
